metadata.title: An odd-period pedal-antipedal area invariant in elliptic billiards
metadata.description: We prove the k403,a observation of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller: the signed area product of the original orbit's origin pedal and origin antipedal is phase independent for every primitive least odd period in a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strict confocal elliptical caustic. All admitted coprime stars are included and every real antipedal intersection is finite. The construction-specific proof distinguishes coincident and opposite complex endpoints, cancels incident double poles and identifies the odd-period quotient lattice. The earlier credited origin-pedal trace supplies the complementary factor. A direct circular extension and an exact same-caustic four-periodic counterexample delimit the theorem. The verification archive contains the standalone LaTeX source, exact algebra and reflected-orbit certificates, independent high-precision geometry and near-pole diagnostics, full receipt comparisons, source hashes, mathematical audits and bounded priority reports. The original observation, prior campaign pedal argument and classical elliptic/cyclic-identity methods are credited. No historical-firstness certificate is claimed. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verification, literature research, coding, writing and internal adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint without external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.

metadata.title: The outer-pedal area centroid in even-period elliptic billiards
metadata.description: We prove the k307 outer-side pedal area-centroid observation of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller for billiards in a noncircular ellipse with a strict confocal elliptic caustic and least even period. The ordered perpendicular feet of any fixed point on the boundary tangent lines have an explicit phase-independent signed area centroid wherever their signed area is nonzero. We classify the entire zero-area locus: none when d is nonnegative, and a fixed circle when d is negative. Simple winding-one even families have a centroid for every fixed point; the four-period value is M/3. An exact primitive eight-period star shows that the exceptional undefined locus is real. The note supplies an all-period support-coordinate and cubic-moment proof. The verification archive contains the LaTeX source, exact symbolic and rational certificates, independent high-precision orbit controls, audit reports and reproducibility instructions. The original observation and classical methods are credited. Bounded primary-source audits found no earlier covering proof, without certifying historical firstness. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, literature research, writing and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint and has not received external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.

metadata.title: Nonunique nearest stable complex quadratics
metadata.description:
For every fixed positive-definite real coefficient inner product, unstable complex quadratics with at least two distinct attained global nearest closed-left-half-plane stable quadratics occur arbitrarily close to z^2, both in monic coefficient space and in the full exact-degree coefficient space. A limiting normal has cubic support against a quartic squared displacement, disproving stable-set prox-regularity; compact localization ensures full-degree global attainment. The same obstruction disproves set prox-regularity of the whole abscissa epigraph. The monic quadratic abscissa nevertheless is function prox-regular at the origin relative to each finite limiting subgradient, with constants depending on that subgradient in the real Euclidean coefficient metric.

This gives a negative answer in degree two to Lewis's historical question about the stable complex monic set. The later Oberwolfach Question1 omits the coefficient field, normalization and metric; its complex convention is explicitly qualified. The note credits Bottema and Kirillov-Overton classical stability-boundary geometry, Burke-Overton/Lewis first-order root analysis, the Poliquin-Rockafellar-Thibault projection characterization, and earlier nearest-polynomial approximation work of Moses-Liu and Orban de Xivry. No real-only or all-degree classification, explicit unstable input and minimizing pair, general nonlinear parameter-metric transfer, firstness or present-day openness guarantee is claimed. The limiting support covector is horizontal; the representing normal vector need not be horizontal in mixed coefficient-height metrics.

The verification archive supplies the complete standalone LaTeX source, a Python-standard-library verifier with 2,005 exact rational assertions and complete expected output, deterministic high-precision function-boundary controls, authored source and bounded-priority notes, publication metadata, license and file hashes. Finite checks supplement the written analytic limiting-normal, every-fixed-metric and global projection proofs. The priority comparison records actual primary-body read extents and remaining access and historical-priority gaps; it is not an exhaustive absence certificate.

AI tools were used extensively in deriving, repairing, literature auditing, reproducing, writing and independent adversarial checking. This is an unrefereed preprint without independent human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification. The named author is responsible for the claims and citations. No outside individual was contacted.

metadata.title: A fixed moment separator without a rational normalized sum-of-squares certificate
metadata.description:
This research note exhibits the phenomenon asked about in the literal fixed-polynomial certificate question in Oberwolfach Report 14/2023, under an explicit rational polynomial-square convention. On the rational unit ball in three variables, p=1+f for Scheiderer's classical quartic has minimum one and annihilates an explicit rational degree-four moment vector of mass one. It belongs to 1+Q_R(g) but not to 1+Q_Q(g), even with arbitrary finite multiplier degrees. The input moment matrix is not positive semidefinite. A different polynomial q=1+x^4 certifies the same vector rationally, p itself is rationally positivity-certifiable, and every rational rescaling cp with c>1 has a rational normalized certificate. The result is outside the companion preprint's strict-margin regime and asserts no algorithm, minimal degree or general descent theorem.

The contribution is an explicit normalized-moment application and scope clarification of established ingredients. Scheiderer's quartic and field obstruction, the classical leading-form/completion mechanism, Benoist's formal-ring observation, Nie's earlier ball application, the prior irrational Gram and Naldi-Sinn semidefinite-infeasibility applications, and Powers' strictly positive rational certificate are credited. The portable archive supplies the manuscript source, all 35 exact rational moments and sparse polynomial data, a Python-standard-library checker with its complete byte-identical expected 2,059-check output, claim and priority notes, publication metadata, source-version provenance and a file-hash manifest. Finite computations supplement the written Galois and all-degree local proofs; they are not finite-search proofs of arbitrary-degree impossibility.

Three independently initiated bounded priority families identified no exact earlier normalized-moment application in the primary passages inspected. Their actual reading extents, unavailable or unexamined final and duplicate bodies, and the unknown remainder and Appendix B.1 statement of the differing 2026 corrected descent proof are disclosed. No worldwide-firstness, current-openness or originating-author-intent guarantee is claimed.
